subject: physics
title: Potential difference, energy and power
key_idea: Potential difference is the energy transferred per unit charge, so W = VQ. The same idea gives eV = ½mv² for an accelerated charge and the power equations P = VI, P = I²R and P = V²/R. The kilowatt-hour is a unit of energy.

blocks.text: A charge moving through a component transfers energy. Potential difference measures how much energy each coulomb transfers.

items.meaning: The energy transferred per unit charge as charge moves between two points. Electrical energy is changed to other forms.
The unit of p.d. One volt is one joule of energy transferred per coulomb of charge: 1 V = 1 J/C.

items: A source of e.m.f. E does work W = EQ on the charge that it drives round a circuit.
The difference between e.m.f. and p.d. is covered in the note on e.m.f. and internal resistance.

diagram.alt: Calculate the energy transferred when a charge moves through a potential difference.
diagram.question: A charge of {Q} C passes through a component with a potential difference of {V} V across it. Calculate the energy transferred.

items: p.d. is energy transferred per unit charge: V = W / Q.
W = VQ gives the energy transferred.

blocks.text: A charged particle accelerated through a p.d. gains kinetic energy equal to the energy transferred to it.

blocks.label: Charge accelerated from rest through a p.d.
where: e = charge on the particle (C), for an electron 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C

items: The energy transferred is W = eV. It becomes kinetic energy, ½mv².
This works for electrons and for any other charged particle. Use that particle's own charge and mass.
The speed rises with the square root of the p.d., so quadrupling V only doubles v.

diagram.alt: Change the accelerating potential difference to see the speed gained by an electron starting from rest.

items: Energy gained = eV, all as kinetic energy for a charge starting from rest.
v = √(2eV / m), so a lighter particle reaches a higher speed.

blocks.text: Power is the rate of energy transfer. Combining P = VI with V = IR gives two more forms.

blocks.label: Energy transferred in a time t

items.text: W = VQ and Q = It, so W = VIt.
Using V = IR gives P = I²R. Use this when the current is known.
Using I = V / R gives P = V²/R. Use this when the p.d. is known.

sections.heading: The kilowatt-hour and the cost of energy

blocks.text: Electricity suppliers charge for energy in kilowatt-hours, not joules.

items.meaning: The energy transferred by a 1 kW device in 1 hour: 1 kW h = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.

blocks.label: Cost
blocks.formula: cost = energy (kW h) × price per kW h

items: To convert kW h to joules, multiply by 3.6 × 10⁶.
A 3 kW heater on for 2 hours transfers 6 kW h. At 30p per kW h it costs £1.80.
Cost = kilowatts × hours × price per kW h.

checks.q: Define potential difference and state what one volt means.
checks.a: The energy transferred per unit charge as it moves between two points. One volt is one joule per coulomb.
